title: Jakab and the Oats
lines: I will tell you a tale about little Jakab, so listen!
Once upon a time, beyond the far beyond, where the short-tailed piglet digs,
there lived a farmer, and he had a little servant lad named Jakab.
One day the farmer said to Jakab: "Go, my son Jakab, to the field and cut the oats!"
Jakab went, but the little rascal did not cut the oats.
No, he did not cut them, and he did not even poke his nose back home.
The farmer got angry and sent the puppy to bite Jakab.
Well, the puppy did not bite Jakab, and Jakab did not cut the oats.
So the farmer sent the stick to beat the puppy.
But the stick did not beat the puppy,
the puppy did not bite Jakab, and Jakab did not cut the oats.
The farmer got even angrier, and he sent the fire
to burn the disobedient stick.
But the fire did not burn the stick, the stick did not beat the puppy,
the puppy did not bite Jakab, and Jakab did not cut the oats.
"Oh, you good-for-nothings!" cried the farmer. "Just you wait!"
At once he sent the water to put out the fire.
Oh, but the water did not put out the fire, the fire did not burn the stick,
the stick did not beat the puppy,
the puppy did not bite Jakab, and Jakab did not cut the oats.
"Is that so?!
Just you wait!"
At once he sent the bull to drink up the water.
But the bull did not drink up the water,
the water did not put out the fire, the fire did not burn the stick,
the stick did not beat the puppy,
the puppy did not bite Jakab, and Jakab did not cut the oats.
Hmm, hmm, what should he do, what should he do?!
Aha, he had it!
He sent the butcher to slaughter the bull.
The butcher went, but he did not slaughter the bull,
the bull did not drink up the water, the water did not put out the fire,
the fire did not burn the stick, the stick did not beat the puppy,
the puppy did not bite Jakab, and Jakab did not cut the oats.
Well, that was all the farmer needed:
he sent the magistrate to have the butcher whipped.
And the magistrate had the butcher whipped, the butcher slaughtered the bull,
the bull drank up the water, the water put out the fire, the fire burned the stick,
the stick beat the puppy, the puppy bit Jakab,
and Jakab cut the oats at once, so well that not a single stalk was left.
If just one stalk of oats had been left, my tale would have gone on longer too.
